How it works

How it works

Kai and Maya have two cards. Each card has two different stories.

Kai’s story is complete on Kai’s card and has gaps on Maya’s.

Maya’s story is complete on Maya’s card and has gaps on Kai’s.

So each one has the answers the other one needs. The only way to get them is to ask.

The two cards

This is what Kai and Maya have in their hands. Click a gap on one card to see where the answer is: always on the other card.

Student A · KaiKai’s card
1Your storyComplete · you answer
1 minute · read it first, in silence

On Saturday I went to the park with my dad. We played soccer for an hour. At three o’clock it started to rain, so we ran home.

2Maya’s storyWith gaps · you ask

On Saturday I went to the park too. I had [what?] with my mom. We left at [when?], because my mom had to work.

Last question · together

Did Maya get wet in the rain?

Student B · MayaMaya’s card
1Your storyComplete · you answer
1 minute · read it first, in silence

On Saturday I went to the park too. I had a picnic with my mom. We left at two o’clock, because my mom had to work.

2Kai’s storyWith gaps · you ask

On Saturday I went to the park with my dad. We played [what?] for an hour. At [when?] it started to rain, so we ran home.

Last question · together

Did Maya get wet in the rain?

Together

Write the answer to the last question.

No. Maya left at two o’clock, and the rain started at three.
